messages:
ben_runtime: heads up — AtlasSearch filed a P99 complaint for their /generate route. Reported time window: ~02:00-03:15 UTC. They say latency jumps ~4x and tail correlates with requests that include a new `X-Session-Id` header coming from their customers.

marta_support: customer provided traces and a flame graph. I pasted the sample span here: 
`service=redwood-runtime route=/generate model=redwood/7B seq=512 token_cost=... p99=1.9s (baseline 450ms)`

alice_sre: can we get KV cache miss rate and key cardinality for that timeframe?

ben_runtime: pulling metrics now — early look: prefix_cache_miss_rate jumped from 6% -> 44% for tenant atlassearch between 02:05-02:40. Also seeing 10x increase in distinct prefix keys/min.

tyler_eng: that screams high-cardinality prefix keys. Any recent deploys or SDK changes?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: client-sdk v2.3.4 -> v2.3.5 at 01:50 UTC (atlassearch/org/atlas-prod) :rocket:

marta_support: customer confirms they upgraded to v2.3.5 yesterday. They said this release started injecting a short-lived `session_id` into request headers for telemetry.

ben_runtime: aha — SDK change note: "add X-Session-Id for tracing". Looks like our prefix key builder pulls request headers into the prefix key if present in `prefix_headers` allowlist. I see `X-Session-Id` was not sanitized and ended up in the prefix key string for this tenant.

alice_sre: evidence from logs: 
```
2026-03-17T02:07:12Z tenant=atlassearch prefix_key="tenant:atlassearch|route:/generate|X-Session-Id:ab12cd34ef" hit=false
2026-03-17T02:07:13Z tenant=atlassearch prefix_key="tenant:atlassearch|route:/generate|X-Session-Id:ff78aa00bb" hit=false
2026-03-17T02:07:14Z tenant=atlassearch prefix_key="tenant:atlassearch|route:/generate|X-Session-Id:9933aa2211" hit=false
```

tyler_eng: that's brutal — session ids are high-cardinality and ephemeral. Cache warms per prefix key, so we got cache fragmentation: the warmup threads are spread across many keys, each with tiny volume, causing overall cache miss surge and backend latency.

ben_runtime: repro locally by running a loop with varied X-Session-Id headers. Quick script: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Session-Id: $RANDOM$RANDOM" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
done
```

marta_support: did a quick smoke in staging with similar loop — reproduced p95 climb and prefix miss rate spike.

alice_sre: immediate mitigation options?

tyler_eng: short-term: deploy a server-side normalization that strips `X-Session-Id` from keys for any tenant that hasn't explicitly allowed it. We can push a hotfix to prefix key builder to ignore headers matching `(?i)^x-session-?id$`.

ben_runtime: agree. Also rolling out a temporary rule in routing: if tenant==atlassearch, treat prefix_key as tenant:atlassearch|route:/generate only (force single normalized key) to let cache warm fast. That reduces fragmentation while we do a proper fix.

deploy-bot: hotfix branch: runtime/prefix-normalize-1765 created. CI green. Can deploy to canary.

marta_support: I've asked AtlasSearch to roll back to v2.3.4 while we validate, they declined but are open to client-side guard rails.

alice_sre: medium-term: add metric prefix_key_cardinality_by_tenant and alert if cardinality/min > 100 over 5m. Also add a small LRU bloom-based sampler to detect ephemeral header values and auto-blacklist them from prefix construction.

tyler_eng: we should also update SDK docs and add a client warning: don't add dynamic session IDs to headers that feed into server-side cache keys. Good to have a safe default on the server to ignore unknown high-cardinality headers.

ben_runtime: action items: 
- TYLER: push prefix normalization hotfix to canary (in progress)
- ALICE: create alert and add cardinality metric (priority P1)
- MARTA: coordinate with AtlasSearch — recommend client change and explain mitigations
- BEN: run simulated load to validate p95/p99 back to baseline after hotfix

tyler_eng: canary deployed to 10% at 02:48 UTC. Early telemetry: prefix miss rate for atlassearch dropped from 44% -> 9% and p99 trending down. :thumbsup:

marta_support: customer ops updated — they see reduced user errors and reported improved responsiveness in a small cohort.

alice_sre: follow-up: we'll keep canary for 2h then promote. Also schedule a postmortem doc: root cause = server-side prefix key inclusion of unstable headers + client SDK rollout that added `X-Session-Id`.

ben_runtime: adding notes to the incident ticket. If anyone has more logs or repro scripts, drop here. Thanks all. :heart:
